data.narrative:
Deepnight, a seed-stage defense and security company founded by Lucas Young and Thomas Li, has raised $5.5M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of ten private and two public companies operating in the Defense & Security sector, including peers such as UFORCE, Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Shield AI.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $5.5M raised as a value proxy and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage progression, implies a valuation of $14M. Peer-median analysis, anchored to three same-sector and same/adjacent-stage comparables, produced a median valuation of $400M, with a range spanning $125M (NODA AI, Series A) to $1.0B (UFORCE, Seed). The peer-median reflects material dispersion within the cohort, reflecting heterogeneity in stage and capital efficiency.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $12M (low) to $460M (high), with a median of $207M. The wide dispersion between stage-progression and peer-median methods reflects tension between capitalization-based and market-comparable approaches at seed stage. Key uncertainties include early-stage monetization traction, competitive differentiation relative to better-capitalized peers, and the degree to which the peer set's broad valuation range reflects comparable risk profiles to Deepnight.
